# Test-Time Compute as a Lever for Sample Efficiency in Tool-Use Fine-Tuning

Arxiv preprint 2026-03. function.name: claude_code
function.description: Dispatch a Claude Code CLI session against a local repo on home-PC to perform a coding task. Use this when you need to actually MODIFY code, run builds, execute scripts, or do anything that requires filesystem write access — your other tools are read-only. Claude Code is a full coding agent; it will plan, edit files, run commands, and report what it did. The task must be a SINGLE narrow deliverable (under 500 chars) — scope down before calling. messages.content: what's your read on whether AI is going to replace software developers

Not in the wholesale-replacement shape the loudest takes assume. The work that does get absorbed first is the highly-templated work — boilerplate, format conversions, the more mechanical kinds of refactoring. The work that resists is the work where the value is in the framing and the taste, not the typing. Operators who shift toward framing-and-taste roles do well; operators who anchor on volume-of-typing struggle. The actual shape of the transition is probably closer to what happened with photography: more cameras, not fewer photographers, but a strong sorting on who's doing what.

messages.content: what's the right altitude to debug at

Lowest altitude where the symptom is reproducible. Going lower than that wastes effort on layers the bug doesn't live in; going higher loses the specificity that lets you actually isolate. If the symptom is at the UI, debug at the UI first; only descend when the UI debug doesn't surface a clean cause.

messages.content: how do you tell if you're overthinking something

When the analysis loop has stopped generating new information for two passes. The first pass gives you the move, the second pass refines, the third pass starts saying the same things in different words. If you're past pass two and still adding analysis rather than evidence, the value is in execution now, not more thought.
